Use case: stylized-concept.
Create a large polished landscape comparison board for FALL, a medieval Spanish-suit card game, approximately 3000 x 2300 pixels. THREE horizontal rows of FIVE equal portrait playing cards (63:88 ratio) fully visible on a quiet dark slate backdrop, front-on orthographic, no perspective or overlap. Clear gutters and row labels above. All rows use the SAME restrained matte illustrative rendering combining clean ink contours and selective gouache shading, so differences must come from actual DESIGN and subject identity, NOT merely rendering technique or color.
Exact row headings: "01  MOUNTAIN KEEP", "02  MARITIME GUILD", "03  MOONLIT GROVE". Small footer "FALL / THREE DISTINCT DECK IDENTITIES".
Each row five subjects in same order: ace of coins (1); three of cups (3, exactly three vessels); seven of clubs (7, exactly seven wooden clubs arranged 2 / 3 / 2); king of swords (12); one shared card back. Small readable top-left rank and suit glyph, rotated matching bottom-right index. Spanish suits only: coins, cups, swords, wooden clubs, not French suits.
DESIGN IDENTITY 1 MOUNTAIN KEEP: grounded medieval mountain fortress. Coin is a heavy octagonal minted brass coin with an original twin mountain relief and squared mint rim. Cups are squat opaque pewter drinking tankards with broad handles and brass bands, utterly unlike stemmed wine chalices. Clubs are stout angular hewn oak cudgels with squared iron bands. King is an elderly broad-shouldered fortress ruler with cropped gray beard, square iron crown, wool mantle and a broad straight arming sword; full clear upper body, do not copy commercial card figures. Border has spare squared masonry corner geometry. Back is charcoal/slate with brass interlocking angular fortress battlements and paired opposing mountain emblems, no text, visibly rotational symmetry.
DESIGN IDENTITY 2 MARITIME GUILD: medieval coastal merchant republic, NOT pirate cliche. Coin is circular silver with scalloped rim, original compass rose relief and a small wave, NO MOUNTAINS. Cups are transparent pale sea-glass goblets, tall delicate narrow stems, clear reflective glass bowl and visible rim with subtle sea-green tint; exactly three separated glass vessels, bright enough against pale paper. Clubs are seven substantial wooden belaying pins with smooth bulbous heads and rope-wrapped grips, read as wooden clubs, NOT oars, wands or swords. King is a clean-shaven dark-skinned middle-aged maritime sovereign with curly hair, a low circlet set with a blue stone, layered ivory linen and slate sea-coat, holding a slender slightly curved single-edged sword; absolutely different face, pose, silhouette, costume and weapon from row 1. Border is fine braided rope and spare wave corner motifs. Back is deep marine blue with opposing compass roses and an interlaced rope-and-wave pattern; no ship silhouette or directional text, visibly 180-degree symmetric.
DESIGN IDENTITY 3 MOONLIT GROVE: quiet folkloric woodland court, grounded crafted materials, no glowing effects. Coin is a round hammered bronze piece with irregular hand-struck rim and a crescent moon embracing an acorn relief, NO MOUNTAINS and NO COMPASS. Cups are three broad handleless hand-carved wooden drinking bowls with flared rims and shallow pedestal feet, pale interior and dark bark exterior, carved leaf motifs; they must look like drinking vessels with open hollow bowls, NOT tankards, glassware or chalices. Clubs are seven crooked knotted blackthorn cudgels with rounded root-ball heads and minimal leather grip, emphatically distinct silhouettes from the other two rows. King is a youthful long-haired woodland ruler with clean-shaven face and a crown of forged bronze leaves, moss-green layered cloak and a narrow leaf-shaped bronze sword. Clearly different posture and character from the other two rulers. Border is slender abstract intertwining roots and leaf corner details. Back is forest green with opposing bronze crescent-acorn medallions and mirrored branching roots, no lettering, visibly 180-degree symmetric.
Keep ivory card faces clear and high contrast. Give EACH identity its own emblem system, silhouettes, materials, costume language, frame construction and back pattern. Do NOT repeat a mountain coin, a familiar stemmed metal goblet, or the same king between rows. No stock deck references, no tracing Fournier, no commercial logos or watermark. Avoid glossy 3D, overly ornate baroque details, magical particle effects or scene backgrounds inside faces. The board must communicate THREE DIFFERENT DECK DESIGNS, not three filters on one deck. Concept preview only, never production sprites.
outputs.notes: User approved the three identities. Not a source sprite sheet; no production art may be extracted from it.
